value.body: The MFA is a two-year postgraduate degree in fine arts. Specialisations include painting, sculpture, applied art, printmaking, art history and visual communication, depending on the university. Most of the time goes to studio practice, with art history and a final display or dissertation.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Usually a BFA (or equivalent) in the relevant specialisation, with a minimum percentage. Admission is through a university entrance or practical test, portfolio review and/or interview; some universities use CUET-PG.

value.title: At a glance
items: Independent practice — exhibitions, commissions, sales — can mean irregular income.
College teaching usually also needs UGC-NET or a PhD; school art teaching may need a B.Ed or a teacher-eligibility test, by state.
Industry routes include illustration, animation, design studios, galleries and art education.
Residencies and grants exist but are competitive.
